title: Firehouse Turkey & White Bean Soup
seoTitle: Firehouse Turkey & White Bean Soup | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: A hearty, lower-fat soup built on lean ground turkey, white beans, and greens
subtitle: A hearty, lower-fat soup built on lean ground turkey, white beans, and greens
description: Ground turkey browns with onion, carrot, and celery, then simmers with white beans, chicken broth, and kale into a thick, ladle-able soup. It is a lighter alternative to the hall's cream-based soup nights.

steps.title: Brown the turkey
steps.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large pot over medium-high. Brown ground turkey in batches 6–7 minutes per batch, breaking it into crumbles, until no pink remains. Set aside.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.instruction: Add remaining oil to the same pot with onion, carrots, and celery. Cook 6–7 minutes until softened, then add garlic and cook 1 more minute.

steps.title: Build the soup base
steps.instruction: Return turkey to the pot along with chicken broth, cannellini beans, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Simmer to develop flavor
steps.instruction: Simmer uncovered 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the broth has thickened slightly from the beans breaking down at the edges.

steps.title: Finish with kale
steps.instruction: Remove the bay leaf. Stir in kale during the last 3–4 minutes just until wilted and bright green — overcooking turns it dull and bitter.

steps.title: Hold and serve
steps.instruction: Keep the soup at a bare simmer for holding, stirring occasionally. Serve with parmesan on the side if using.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover turkey and white bean soup — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool turkey and white bean soup and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Brown the turkey in batches — crowding the pot steams it instead of browning it.
Rookie tip: Add kale at the very end; it only needs a few minutes to wilt properly.
This soup thickens overnight — add extra broth when reheating leftovers.
Swap kale for spinach if that's what's on hand; add it off heat since spinach wilts almost instantly.
tonightSpread: Main: Turkey and white bean soup
Sides: Crusty bread, simple green salad
Condiments: Grated parmesan, red pepper flakes
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool turkey and white bean soup in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Freezes well in individual portions for up to 3 months.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It still feels like a real cold-weather soup night, holds well in a big pot for staggered eating, and comes in noticeably lighter than a cream-based chowder without sacrificing how filling it is.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: this soup holds and reheats exceptionally well. Storage: refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheating: reheat covered on the stove, adding a splash of broth since it thickens as it sits.
substitutions: Use ground chicken instead of turkey.
Use great northern beans or navy beans instead of cannellini beans.
